query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: is_travel
per_column.rationale: Whether an expense is travel-related is a precondition/scope filter for the concept, not an aspect OF the risk itself. It gates applicability rather than carving the risk into parts.

per_column.name: policy_risks
per_column.rationale: This column enumerates the risk types (High Amount, Unresolved Status, International/Premium Travel) as a bundled multi-label field. It restates the whole concept as an aggregated list rather than exposing a single non-overlapping facet; internally it conflates several distinct risk dimensions into one column.

per_column.name: amount_tier
per_column.rationale: Amount magnitude is a genuine constitutive aspect of travel policy risk (excessive spend is a risk dimension). It captures the 'monetary threshold' facet of the concept.

judge.rationale: Only one column (amount_tier) is a clean single facet of the concept. is_travel is a scope predictor, not a part of the risk. policy_risks is a bundled restatement of the entire concept that itself packs multiple distinct aspects (monetary excess, status/approval, travel class, international) into one multi-label field, which both overlaps heavily with amount_tier (High Amount vs High tier) and violates a proper MECE decomposition into separate columns. As a facet SET, the decomposition is weak: it does not carve travel_policy_risk into distinct non-overlapping facet columns (mutual exclusivity is undermined by the amount overlap and the bundling), and it leaves major constitutive aspects (approval/documentation compliance, booking-class/premium violations, timeliness, vendor/booking-channel compliance) either merged inside one column or absent, hurting exhaustiveness.
